thread.title: CURRENCIES : Dollar Mixed Ahead Of Jobs Report, Powell Remarks | MarketScreener

author: www.4-traders.com
title: CURRENCIES : Dollar Mixed Ahead Of Jobs Report, Powell Remarks | MarketScreener
text:
By William Watts, MarketWatch
The U.S. dollar Friday morning in New York put in a mixed performance versus major rivals as investors awaited U.S. jobs data and remarks by Federal Reserve Chairman Jerome Powell and as investor appetite for assets perceived as risky got a lift after the People's Bank of China cut its reserve requirements.
The ICE U.S. Dollar Index , a measure of the U.S. currency against a basket of six major rivals, was off 0.1% at 96.193 and was headed for a flat performance for the week.
Forward rates "imply the hurdle for positive data surprises supporting USD is low, though one payrolls report probably would not be sufficient to shift sentiment much," said Adam Cole, chief currency strategist at RBC Capital Markets in a note. "Fed Chair Powell will need tread a careful path between acknowledging some further softness in the data and not feeding negative sentiment."
China's Commerce Ministry confirmed that a delegation of U.S. officials will travel to Beijing for a new round of trade talks on Monday and Tuesday, according to news reports.
Sentiment also got a boost after China's central bank on Friday cut the ratio of cash that banks must hold as reserves by 100 basis points, or 1%, according to news reports -- a move that has been seen as a means to help reduce the risk of a sharper slowdown in the world's second-largest economy.
The December jobs report is set for release at 8:30 a.m. Eastern Time, while Powell is set to take part in a panel discussion alongside his predecessors Janet Yellen and Ben Bernanke at an event in Atlanta at 10:15 a.m. The employment report is expected to show the U.S. economy added 182,000 new jobs in December, according to a MarketWatch survey of economists.
The dollar weakened Thursday as a sharp selloff on Wall Street following a warning from Apple Inc.(AAPL) and downbeat manufacturing survey data from China, the eurozone and the U.S. Global stocks were buoyed Friday, with stock-index futures pointing to a positive start for Wall Street.
On Friday, the euro changed hands at $1.1404, up from $1.1395 late Monday. The British pound traded at $1.2672 versus $1.2634.
On Thursday, the Japanese yen soared in volatile and thin trade in early Asia-Pacific hours following Apple's rare sales forecast cut. The dollar rose to 108.05 yen, up from 107.66 late Thursday.
